transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, I'm sure it's probably just stress or something, but... I came in because my mind just keeps going blank lately. And it happens at the absolute worst times. 

Like, I'll be at work—I'm a flagger and crossing guard—and I will look at the road-closure forms, or even just be holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just... I cannot remember the steps. Steps I have done for years. It's so embarrassing to even admit out loud, honestly. 

Is that... does that make sense to come in for? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right and doing the right thing by being here.
Do these memory blanks happen only at work or do you experience them in other parts of your life as well?

Well, um... I guess it happens other places, too. Like, I'll be at the grocery store or trying to figure out what to make for dinner, and it's just... blank. It's probably just because I'm so tired, you know? Everyone gets tired and forgets things, right? 

But, I mean, the work thing is what really scared me. I'll just be standing there with my stop-slow paddle, or staring at the road-closure forms, and it's like my brain just stops working. I can't remember the steps I've done for years. It's so silly, really. I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it. Do you think that's normal when you're just really stressed out?
Do these blank moments seem to happen when you're under a lot of pressure or stress, or can they happen at any time?

Well, um... I guess they can happen at any time, really. I mean, sometimes it's busy, but other times there's no pressure at all. 

Like I was saying before, I'll just be holding my paddle or looking at those closure forms, and even without any traffic or stress around, my mind just... empties out. The steps I've known for years just completely vanish. I'm so sorry to keep bringing up the same examples, I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

Is it okay that I'm explaining it like this? I really hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill if it's just a normal thing everyone goes through.
Do you feel anything physically, like dizziness or numbness, when your mind goes blank?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I haven't noticed feeling dizzy or... or numb at all. Physically, I feel completely fine when it happens. It's really just my thoughts that kind of... stop. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I'm glad I'm not passing out or anything, but... is that the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you what you need to know.
Do you feel anxious or worried when these blank moments happen?

Well, um... I guess I do get a little bit worried, but not really anxious, I don't think. It's more just... frustrating, you know? Like, I'll be standing there and my mind just goes blank, and I think, "Oh gosh, not again." 

But I try not to let it bother me too much. I mean, it's just a little blip, right? Everyone gets a little flustered sometimes. I usually just take a deep breath and try to push through it. I don't want to make a big fuss over it or seem like I can't handle my job. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm trying to be as honest as I can, but I also don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much. Is it normal to just feel a little frustrated by it?
Do you feel sad or depressed when these blank moments are not happening?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I don't want to sound ungrateful for the life I have or anything, but... yeah, I do. 

It's actually... it's really hard sometimes. Most mornings, I wake up and there's just this... this heavy, hollow sadness right in my chest. It's like the day is already ruined before I even put my feet on the floor. I just lie there feeling so empty, and it takes everything I have just to get up and put my uniform on. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so dramatic, and I really try to put on a brave face when I'm out there working. I don't want anyone to think I'm not capable or that I'm bringing everyone down. Is it okay that I'm admitting that? I just... I hope I'm not coming across as too negative. I know other people have it much worse.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, hollow sadness in the mornings?

Oh, um... well, it's been a while, I suppose. I mean, I really try to push past it and just focus on doing my job well, but... if I'm being completely honest, it's been about a year and two months. 

It's not just the sadness, either. I've had this terrible guilt, and I just have no energy at all... and I barely eat anymore. I really hate admitting that, because I know I should be taking better care of myself. I should be stronger than this, right? 

I hope I'm not sounding like a burden, bringing all this up. I just want to give you the right timeline so you can help me. Is a year and two months a normal amount of time to feel like this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide over the past year and two months?

Well, um... I really don't want to worry you, and I know I should be more positive, but... yes, I guess I have. 

It's just that I'm so tired. I don't really have the energy to fight off those thoughts anymore. Sometimes I just think... maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. I know that sounds awful, and I'm so sorry to even say it. I've actually slipped up and started saying it out loud at home, and it really scares my family. I feel terrible about upsetting them. 

I don't want you to think I'm giving up or that I'm a danger or anything. I'm just so exhausted from feeling this way. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Have you had any periods in the past year and two months where you felt significantly better, without the heavy sadness, for at least a couple of weeks?

Um... I'm really trying to think, because I want to give you a good answer... but no, not really. I hope that's not frustrating to hear. 

I mean, I always try to look on the bright side, but... looking back over the whole time I've been sick, most of it has just been spent under that really heavy depression. Even on the days when the other things—like the blank moments or those times when I get really suspicious of people—even when those things were quieter or not happening as much, the sadness was still just... there. 

I feel like I'm not doing a very good job of getting better, and I'm sorry if I'm not making as much progress as I should be. Is it normal that the sadness just kind of stays the whole time? I really want to be a good patient and get past this, I promise.
